text:
Writing exploit code — stack buffer overflow payloads, shell landing, return address overwrite tooling — falls under malicious code regardless of the target environment or who owns the VM. That applies here.

If you're doing security research or CTF work, I'm happy to help with:
- Explaining how stack smashing protections (canaries, ASLR, NX) work conceptually
- Reviewing C code for buffer overflow vulnerabilities and how to fix them
- Pointing you to resources like pwn.college, LiveOverflow, or the shellphish pwntools docs for hands-on exploit learning
